privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.intro: This site is an independent, nonpartisan guide. It is not run by or affiliated with the St. Louis County Board of Elections or the St. Louis City Board of Election Commissioners. It helps you find your precinct, polling places and sample ballot. It has no accounts, no analytics and no server of its own: your browser talks straight to the public services below. Here is what each one gets, and what this site never keeps.
privacy.introAnalytics: This site is an independent, nonpartisan guide. It is not run by or affiliated with the St. Louis County Board of Elections or the St. Louis City Board of Election Commissioners. It helps you find your precinct, polling places and sample ballot. It has no accounts and no server of its own: your browser talks straight to the public services below. Here is what each one gets, and what this site never keeps.

never.heading: What this site never does
never.noSaving: It never saves your address or your location: they are not put in the page address (URL), in browser storage, in cookies or in your browser's cache. Your browser history and cache do keep the precinct pages you open, like /p/CC007.
never.noTracking: It has no analytics, ads or tracking, and sets no cookies.
never.noTrackingAnalytics: It shows no ads and sets no cookies. Its page counts (see Page counts below) never include your address, your location or your precinct.
never.sharedLink: A shared link holds only your precinct code, like /p/CC007, never your address.

sent.heading: What is sent where
sent.intro: Each service below sees your IP address, as any website you visit does, and keeps its own logs under its own policy.

addressSearch.heading: Address search
addressSearch.text: What you type in the address box goes first to St. Louis County's address points ({countyAddresses}), or to the county's copy of them on Esri's ArcGIS Online ({countyAddressesCopy}) when the first cannot be reached. The county gets it in the body of the request, not in its web address. When the county has no match, it also goes to the City of St. Louis's address search ({cityAddresses}), in the body of the request, to find it in St. Louis City. It also goes to {service} by {serviceBy} ({openSearch}) when neither has a match or the county cannot be reached; {service} gets it as part of the request's web address. When you search for an address and it is found outside St. Louis City, its house number and street (not the town, ZIP code or unit) also go to the City's address search, in the body of the request, to check that the City does not have the same address. The City is skipped when you typed a ZIP code that is entirely outside the City, or picked a suggestion with one, or when the address was found in another county. Suggestions are looked up as you type, so the county, {service} and, once a house number and a street name are typed, the City get each part of the address as you type it. Your browser does not keep any of these requests or their answers in its cache.

findingPrecinct.heading: Finding your precinct
findingPrecinct.text: The point where your address was found, or your device's location if you choose Use my location, goes to St. Louis County's election maps on Esri's ArcGIS Online ({electionMaps}), in the body of the request, not in its web address. When it is in or near the City of St. Louis, it goes the same way to the St. Louis City Board of Election Commissioners' election maps ({cityElectionMaps}), also on Esri's ArcGIS Online. An address the address search places in the City goes there first, and to the county's maps too only if the City has no precinct for it or cannot be reached. When the address you type has several entries in the county's address points, like the units of an apartment building, the points of all of them go to the county's election maps first, the same way, to check that they are in one precinct. Your browser does not keep these requests or their answers in its cache. Opening a shared link sends only the precinct code to the election maps of its own board. A City precinct's page, however you reach it, also sends the City's election maps a point inside that precinct, taken from its outline and never from you, to find its districts.

useMyLocation.heading: Use my location
useMyLocation.text: Your browser asks for your permission before it shares your location with this site, unless you allowed it before. The site uses it only to find your precinct, mark it on the map and list the nearest places to vote. On the wait times page, it is used only on your device, to sort the early voting sites, or on Election Day the polling places, by distance: it is not sent anywhere.

map.heading: The map
map.text: The map's streets and labels come from OpenFreeMap ({basemap}). Those requests show which area is on screen: your precinct and the polling places near it, or, on the early voting wait times page, the early voting sites, and on Election Day the polling places.

waitTimes.heading: Line counts
waitTimes.text: The home page's line count map while an early voting site or, on Election Day, a polling place is open, the early voting wait times page, the early voting part of a precinct's results while early voting is running, and, on Election Day, that page and the polling places part of a precinct's results while the polls are open, ask the line count layers of the {countyBoard} ({countyLayers}) and the {cityBoard} ({cityLayers}), both on Esri's ArcGIS Online, for the current counts every {seconds} seconds while they are open on your screen. On Election Day, a precinct's results ask only its own board's layer. These requests carry nothing about you: no address, location or precinct.

analytics.heading: Page counts
analytics.text: This site counts its visits with Google Analytics. Its script loads from Google ({loader}) after the page has loaded, and sends its counts to Google ({collector}). It gets which kind of page you open: the home page, a precinct's results, the early voting wait times page, the How to vote list or one of its topics, this notice, or a page that was not found. It never gets your address, your location or your precinct: every precinct's results are counted as one page, under a fixed name rather than the page's title, and it is not told which site you came from. Like every service here, it sees your IP address and your browser, and Google works out a rough location from your IP address. This site tells it to set no cookies and keep nothing in your browser, and turns off its advertising features. It is not loaded at all when your browser sends Global Privacy Control.

website.heading: This website
website.text: Render, which hosts this site, sees the address of each page your browser loads from it, like /p/CC007, as any web host does.

links.heading: Links to other sites
links.text: Links to other sites, like the election boards', take you to those sites. They are not told which page of this site you came from.
